facts.label: Leverage and coverage
facts.text: Reported leverage rose from 1.74x at the end of FY2025 to 2.97x on the last twelve months to 2026-09-30 although debt barely moved, so the change is entirely earnings: last-twelve-month reported EBITDA fell from USD 623.3 million to USD 367.0 million because Adjusted EBITDA of USD 66.7 million and USD 96.5 million in the first two quarters of 2026 replaced USD 181.3 million and USD 200.7 million a year earlier, while four drillships returned to work after idle periods. Net leverage rose from 0.78x to 1.54x, and on the issuer's adjusted measure total leverage rose from 1.69x to 2.65x. Creditors are therefore looking at a trailing ratio that overstates current leverage if the 2026 recovery holds and understates it if the recovery stalls. facts.label: Leverage and coverage
facts.text: Within 2026 the trend runs the other way: Adjusted EBITDA was USD 66.7 million in Q1, USD 96.5 million in Q2 and USD 150.6 million in Q3, a rise of more than twofold from Q1, as three drillships started new contracts and a fourth won a higher day rate, and as the war-risk cost drag moderated from about USD 30 million in Q2 to about USD 24 million in Q3. The recovery is therefore operating-led, with revenue efficiency of 97% in Q3, but only the last two quarters show it; the trailing measures should improve as the weak Q4 2025 (Adjusted EBITDA of USD 97.0 million) leaves the last twelve months, if Q4 2026 comes in above that level. Basis: calculation C43; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_a09302026ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 1–3

facts.label: Liquidity
facts.text: Liquidity was USD 900.1 million at 2026-09-30 (cash of USD 525.1 million plus the undrawn USD 375.0 million revolver), against no principal maturity before 2030 and a single bond. facts.label: Subsequent events
facts.text: The October 2026 sale of VALARIS 111 reduces net debt by about USD 7.5 million and lowers pro forma net leverage to 1.51x from 1.54x on reported EBITDA, a small effect. The larger event for creditors is the pending all-stock combination with Transocean, scheduled to close on or about 2026-12-01: the supplied documents do not say how Valaris debt is treated in the transaction, but if a change of control triggering event occurs under the indenture, noteholders may be offered repurchase at 101.0% of principal. limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- Cash interest paid is not stated for any quarter or nine-month period, so EBITDA over cash interest for the last twelve months to 2026-09-30 is not calculable; it restricts cash-based cover for the latest period (High); obtain the supplemental cash flow note of each quarterly report. A proxy on accrued net interest expense is shown instead. - FY2024 Adjusted EBITDA is not stated in the supplied documents, so adjusted leverage and cover for FY2024 are not supplied; it restricts the adjusted trend before FY2025 (Low); obtain the FY2024 earnings release. - Revolver availability at 2024-12-31 is not stated in the supplied annual report, so the undrawn facility for FY2024 is not supplied; it restricts the FY2024 liquidity figure (Low). - Dashes in the source statements (merger and integration expenses, other operating items, share repurchases, debt issuance costs and other financing) are carried as not supplied rather than zero, as the method requires; no total depends on them (Low). - The line for bad debt expense (recovery) is shown separately only in the quarterly and nine-month cash flow statements, so the FY2024 and FY2025 columns are not supplied for it; operating cash flow still adds up in every column (Low). - No financial covenant level, definition or compliance figure is printed for the 2028 Credit Agreement, so no headroom is calculated (High for covenant work, none for leverage); obtain the credit agreement. - No component table separates the USD 11.5 million between principal and carrying value of the notes into discount, premium and issuance costs, so the reconciling item is found by difference (Low). - The statements for Valaris Finance Company LLC and the guarantor subsidiaries are not supplied, so guarantor leverage and structural priority cannot be assessed (Medium). - The effect of the pending Transocean combination on the group's debt, including any repurchase offer for the notes, is not stated, so no pro forma figure for it is given (Medium); revisit after closing. - The 2026-10-30 coupon payment of about USD 46.1 million is a scheduled payment that the supplied documents do not report as made, so it is not reflected in the pro forma net debt (Low). - ARO's full financial statements are not supplied; only a condensed 100% income statement is, so the group's exposure to ARO is limited to the notes receivable, the investment, the earnings line and the newbuild funding commitment (Medium). - Page numbers cited in this analysis are chunk numbers of the supplied text files, not printed page numbers (Low).

facts.label: Business and ownership in credit terms
facts.text: Valaris contracts ultra-deepwater drillships and premium jackups on day rate contracts, so earnings follow rig utilisation and day rates, and a stacked or idle rig earns nothing while its holding costs continue. The group is widely held with no sponsor, which means no committed equity support and no sponsor-driven leakage; the creditors' main exposure is the pending sale to Transocean and the 50% ARO joint venture, which Valaris does not consolidate, so ARO's own debt is outside group net debt and its earnings reach Valaris only as an equity share that Adjusted EBITDA excludes. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)

facts.label: Market forces and external factors
facts.text: Rivalry is strong because contracts are awarded by competitive bid and price is often the deciding factor, and ten drillships across the industry were idle at the end of the third quarter with nine due back to work by early 2027, which could cap day rates; the supply of benign environment floaters has fallen by more than 45% since 2014, which supports them. New entry is limited by high newbuild cost and shipyard capacity, substitutes are other oil supply such as onshore shale and, over time, the energy transition, buyers are a few large oil companies with termination rights, and suppliers (shipyards, insurers, crews) have pushed costs up. Politically, the Middle East conflicts cost about USD 24.0 million of operating income in Q3, and tax disputes and the 15% Bermuda tax add earnings uncertainty. facts.label: Financial profile
facts.text: On the method's nine dimensions the assessment is: scale and market position average, with a fleet the issuer describes as among the largest in the world (13 drillships and 28 jackups owned at 2026-11-03) but a concentrated customer base; competitive advantage average, resting on modern seventh-generation drillships (12 of 13) rather than on contract terms; business diversification weak to average, with floaters 61.1% of backlog; cost and capex flexibility average, because contract-specific capital spending is recoverable but a fixed cost base is not; margin stability average, improving; free cash flow stability weak; ability to refinance average, with one bond due in 2030 and market quotations not supplied beyond the quarter-end fair value; liquidity position strong relative to maturities; and financial policy and governance average, with no sponsor but event risk from the combination. Supports are the contracted base and liquidity; the main constraint is free cash flow. facts.label: Outlook
facts.text: Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the debt-service case depends on drillship restarts continuing: management says day rates are moving higher and deepwater opportunities are converting to contracts. Reinvestment stays high, with USD 117.0 million to USD 142.0 million of capital additions still implied for the fourth quarter, and ARO has ordered four newbuild jackups that Valaris may be asked to help fund. Sector tailwinds are customer emphasis on energy security and deepwater sanctioning (about 65% of expected deepwater activity has breakeven prices below USD 50 a barrel), and headwinds are the Middle East conflicts, cost inflation and war-risk insurance. Over three to five years the 2028 revolver and the 2030 notes fall due, so the outlook for earnings through 2027 decides refinancing terms. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: An issuer-specific downside starts with a customer programme delay or a Middle East shipyard stoppage that returns Adjusted EBITDA to the first-quarter level of USD 66.7 million a quarter; at that level revenue and utilisation fall first, the largely fixed cost base turns the margin gain back, and free cash flow turns more negative because capital additions are committed. Holding that level for four quarters gives Adjusted EBITDA of USD 266.8 million, a coupon cover of 2.90x and a cash outflow of USD 259.6 million after the coupon and capital additions, so cash falls from USD 525.1 million at 2026-09-30 to USD 265.5 million, liquidity to USD 640.5 million and net leverage rises to 3.08x. Management can slow discretionary capital additions and sell stacked rigs, as it did in 2026, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress within twelve months, but the margin for the 2028 revolver renewal narrows and the revolver's covenants, whose levels are not printed, could become the binding constraint. Basis: calculation K3; calculation K4; calculation K5; calculation K6; calculation K7; calculation K8; calculation K9; calculation F7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22

facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Valaris presents an adequate business profile supported by contracted drillship backlog, modern assets and liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by negative free cash flow, trailing leverage that has risen and concentration in customers and floaters. Cash-flow durability appears adequate only if the third-quarter earnings level holds. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on earnings through 2027 and on how the change of control treats the notes. The primary downside path is a fall back to first-quarter earnings while capital spending stays committed. Further analysis would require the indenture, the credit agreement, the acquirer's disclosure and ARO's accounts. Fundamental credit review completed with limitations. Top risk: negative free cash flow combined with event risk from the change of control. ## Findings
### Bottom line

The seven supplied filings and releases are enough for a credit snapshot of Valaris Ltd, but not for any view that depends on the executed debt documents, which were not supplied. Creditors can rely on the reported statements, debt terms and liquidity; covenant headroom, ratings triggers and recovery cannot be established from these documents.

The evidence is current: the latest report was signed two days before the as-of date and the latest balance sheet is 36 days old. It describes the capital structure before the pending Transocean combination, which is scheduled to close after the as-of date and which may let noteholders put their notes at a premium to par if a change of control triggering event occurs.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Valaris Ltd's trailing leverage is moderate but rising, with total debt at 2.97x last-twelve-month reported EBITDA, and liquidity is ample, so creditors face earnings-recovery risk rather than refinancing risk before the 2030 maturity. Net debt was USD 563.4 million at 2026-09-30, or USD 555.9 million pro forma for the October 2026 rig sale; net leverage was 1.54x, against 0.78x at the end of FY2025.
Basis: calculation C26; calculation C27; calculation C21; calculation C15; calculation C45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21

The recovery is real but recent: Adjusted EBITDA reached USD 150.6 million in Q3, more than twice the USD 66.7 million of Q1, yet nine-month operating cash flow of USD 155.3 million covered under half of capital additions of USD 328.0 million. Cash of USD 525.1 million plus the undrawn USD 375.0 million revolver gives USD 900.1 million of liquidity.

### Leverage and coverage

Reported leverage rose from 1.74x at the end of FY2025 to 2.97x on the last twelve months to 2026-09-30 although debt barely moved, so the change is entirely earnings: last-twelve-month reported EBITDA fell from USD 623.3 million to USD 367.0 million because Adjusted EBITDA of USD 66.7 million and USD 96.5 million in the first two quarters of 2026 replaced USD 181.3 million and USD 200.7 million a year earlier, while four drillships returned to work after idle periods. Net leverage rose from 0.78x to 1.54x, and on the issuer's adjusted measure total leverage rose from 1.69x to 2.65x. Creditors are therefore looking at a trailing ratio that overstates current leverage if the 2026 recovery holds and understates it if the recovery stalls.

Basis: calculation C20; calculation C21; calculation C26; calculation C27; calculation C23; calculation C28; calculation C08; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_a09302026ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1

Within 2026 the trend runs the other way: Adjusted EBITDA was USD 66.7 million in Q1, USD 96.5 million in Q2 and USD 150.6 million in Q3, a rise of more than twofold from Q1, as three drillships started new contracts and a fourth won a higher day rate, and as the war-risk cost drag moderated from about USD 30 million in Q2 to about USD 24 million in Q3. The recovery is therefore operating-led, with revenue efficiency of 97% in Q3, but only the last two quarters show it; the trailing measures should improve as the weak Q4 2025 (Adjusted EBITDA of USD 97.0 million) leaves the last twelve months, if Q4 2026 comes in above that level.
Basis: calculation C43; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_a09302026ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 1–3

Cash interest cover was 6.89x in FY2025 and 6.06x in FY2024 on reported EBITDA, and 7.10x on adjusted EBITDA in FY2025. Cash interest paid is stated only for fiscal years, so cash-based cover for the last twelve months is not calculable; on accrued net interest expense the proxy is 3.74x on reported and 4.19x on adjusted EBITDA, which is thinner than the annual figure but still adequate for a fixed-rate bond whose coupon is about USD 92.1 million a year.
Basis: calculation C22; calculation C19; calculation C25; calculation C30; calculation C31; 10-K_2025-12-31_val-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 153
### Cash flow quality

The group is not self-funding at the current investment rate. In the nine months of 2026 operating cash flow of USD 155.3 million fell short of capital additions of USD 328.0 million, so operating cash flow less capital additions was negative USD 172.7 million against positive USD 236.8 million a year earlier; asset sales of USD 102.6 million and about USD 43.0 million of U.S. tax refunds inside operating cash flow limited the fall in balance-sheet cash to USD 74.3 million. Receivables rose by USD 80.0 million in Q3 and changes in operating assets and liabilities used USD 56.6 million, so working capital absorbed part of the earnings recovery.

Basis: calculation C34; calculation C35; calculation C37; calculation C42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52

The issuer expects 2026 capital additions of USD 445.0 million to USD 470.0 million, which implies USD 117.0 million to USD 142.0 million in the fourth quarter. At the Q3 operating cash flow of USD 67.2 million the fourth quarter would again fall short of capital additions, so operating cash flow less capital additions would stay negative into the year end; this is an inference from the stated range, not a figure the issuer gives.
Basis: calculation C38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52

Contract liabilities (deferred customer revenue) rose from USD 150.9 million to USD 208.0 million over nine months, a USD 57.1 million non-debt funding float that supports cash today and unwinds as the related contracts are performed, so part of the cash balance is customer prepayment rather than earnings.
Basis: calculation C39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29
### Liquidity

Liquidity was USD 900.1 million at 2026-09-30 (cash of USD 525.1 million plus the undrawn USD 375.0 million revolver), against no principal maturity before 2030 and a single bond. Letters of credit and surety bonds of USD 113.7 million are issued outside the revolver, so the full facility is available subject to covenants whose levels are not printed. The unconsolidated ARO joint venture is a contingent call on cash: each partner may be asked for up to USD 1.1 billion of newbuild funding if ARO cannot raise third-party finance, and USD 400.7 million of notes receivable from ARO are due in October 2027 and October 2028 with an expected extension.
### Definitions and data quality

Reported EBITDA is a derived measure (operating income plus depreciation) because the issuer states only Adjusted EBITDA; the difference to the issuer's measure was USD 43.8 million over the last twelve months, mostly merger costs of USD 40.5 million and other operating loss of USD 19.7 million, less USD 16.4 million of equity earnings of ARO. Each stated quarter of Adjusted EBITDA reconciles exactly to the statements, and the last-twelve-month figures agree whether built from year and nine-month stubs or from four quarters. Cash interest paid for interim periods and FY2024 Adjusted EBITDA are not stated anywhere in the supplied documents.
Basis: calculation C44; calculation C10; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_a09302026ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 15
### Subsequent events

The October 2026 sale of VALARIS 111 reduces net debt by about USD 7.5 million and lowers pro forma net leverage to 1.51x from 1.54x on reported EBITDA, a small effect. The larger event for creditors is the pending all-stock combination with Transocean, scheduled to close on or about 2026-12-01: the supplied documents do not say how Valaris debt is treated in the transaction, but if a change of control triggering event occurs under the indenture, noteholders may be offered repurchase at 101.0% of principal. No effect on net debt is stated, so none is estimated.
Basis: calculation C45; calculation C46; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-K_2025-12-31_val-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 127

## Findings
### Bottom line

Valaris is a widely held offshore driller with no controlling shareholder disclosed in the supplied documents, so creditors' main exposure is event risk from the pending all-stock sale to Transocean and from the ARO joint venture, not sponsor extraction. A change of control may let holders of the USD 1,100.0 million second lien notes require repurchase at 101.0% of principal.

The operating base supports debt service for now: contract backlog was USD 4,750.1 million on 2026-11-02, all ten active drillships are on contract, and no shares have been repurchased in 2026 after USD 425.0 million between 2023 and 2025. Four customers each supplied at least 10% of Q3 revenue, and Middle East conflict costs cut Q3 operating income by about USD 24.0 million.

### Key findings

- Ownership offers creditors neither a sponsor backstop nor sponsor leakage. Valaris emerged from bankruptcy in 2021, has paid no dividends, had 63 holders of record in February 2026, and the supplied documents describe no dividend recapitalisation, liability management transaction or related-party fee other than its lease agreements with ARO; the repurchase programme used USD 425.0 million of its USD 600.0 million authorisation, and the source does not state how the repurchases were funded.

- The pending Transocean combination is the principal credit event, and its effect on the notes is not established. The all-stock agreement signed on 2026-02-09 values Valaris at about USD 5.8 billion at announcement, leaves Valaris holders with about 47% of the combined company on a fully diluted basis, and is scheduled to close on or about 2026-12-01; until then the agreement restricts new debt, dividends, repurchases, encumbrances and disposals, and Valaris owes Transocean USD 173.0 million if it ends in specified circumstances. The supplied documents do not say how Valaris debt is treated, and the notes' quoted fair value at 2026-09-30 was 102.3% of principal, above the 101.0% repurchase price, so a repurchase offer would help holders only if prices fall.

- Contract backlog gives revenue visibility but rests mainly on floaters. Floaters hold 61.1% of the USD 4,750.1 million backlog, remaining contract durations run from about 1 month to 4 years, and some contracts allow termination for the customer's convenience or if a final investment decision is not taken.
Basis: calculation C4; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_a09302026ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_val-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10

- Customer and country concentration is material. Four customers contributed 49% of Q3 revenue and Brazil alone 23.1%, so one customer's budget decision or one country's tax or operating event can move earnings.
Basis: calculation C5; calculation C7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31

- ARO is a contingent call on cash rather than a cash source. ARO has made no cash distribution to its partners since formation, Valaris's notes receivable from ARO of USD 400.7 million fall due in October 2027 and October 2028 with an extension expected, and each partner may be asked for up to USD 1.1 billion of newbuild funding; ARO ordered two more rigs in August 2026.

- Asset sales have been recycled into liquidity, not distributions. Cash proceeds from disposals were USD 102.6 million in the first nine months of 2026, no shares were repurchased, and the combination agreement now bars further repurchases and limits further disposals.

- Disclosure supports monitoring but leaves governance and covenant questions open. The 2025 accounts carry an unqualified audit opinion and effective internal control over financial reporting, but the proxy statement, the indenture and the credit agreement were not supplied, and the issuer has said it will give no further guidance updates.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_val-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-K_2025-12-31_val-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-K_2025-12-31_val-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 156; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_a09302026ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 5; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against the view that extraction risk is low is the USD 425.0 million repurchased since 2023 while USD 1,100.0 million of secured notes stayed outstanding, together with USD 175.0 million of programme capacity that remains authorised; the funding source is not stated and the combined company's capital policy is not established. The view would also change if the indenture shows that the notes are repaid, exchanged or left behind a larger secured claim after closing, if a change of control triggering event occurs, if ARO calls capital or its notes receivable are not extended, or if repurchases resume after closing.
### Limitations

- Directors, executive compensation and security ownership are incorporated from a proxy statement that was not supplied, so the finding that no controlling shareholder is disclosed could change if a large holder exists.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_val-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 156

- The indenture and the 2028 Credit Agreement were not supplied, so capacity for restricted payments, asset transfers and priming cannot be assessed; the governance risk level rests on behaviour alone and would move up if the documents give wide capacity.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)

- Neither the treatment of Valaris debt in the transaction nor the leverage of the acquirer is stated in the supplied documents, so the finding that the change of control is the main event risk cannot be sized.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12

- ARO's own financial statements are not supplied beyond a condensed income statement, so the finding that the ARO funding commitment is contingent rather than probable cannot be tested against ARO's cash needs.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Valaris and Transocean Ltd. signed a business combination agreement on 2026-02-09 under which Transocean will acquire all Valaris common shares for 15.235 Transocean shares each, by court-approved scheme of arrangement under Bermudian law; the value was about USD 5.8 billion at announcement and Valaris holders would own about 47% of the combined company on a fully diluted basis. Regulatory approvals have been received, shareholder meetings are scheduled for 2026-11-24, a Bermuda court hearing for 2026-11-26 and closing on or about 2026-12-01, and either party may end the agreement if it has not closed by 2027-02-09, subject to extension. Until closing the agreement restricts new debt, dividends, repurchases, encumbrances and disposals, and Valaris owes Transocean USD 173.0 million if the agreement ends in specified circumstances, with reimbursement of up to USD 58 million of Transocean expenses if Valaris holders fail to approve.

No new debt was issued or repaid in 2026. The capital structure is the USD 1,100.0 million 8.375% second lien notes due 2030-04-30, issued in April and August 2023 by Valaris Limited and Valaris Finance Company LLC and guaranteed by certain subsidiaries, and an undrawn USD 375.0 million revolver due 2028-04-03. Two supplemental indentures were signed on 2026-07-16 and 2026-09-14 and filed as exhibits, naming further Valaris subsidiaries as parties; the documents do not state their purpose. If a change of control triggering event occurs, the issuers may be required to offer to repurchase the notes at 101.0% of principal, but the definition of that event is in the indenture, which was not supplied.

spans.text: ## Request

Valaris Ltd (issuer id val), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the fundamental credit profile of the consolidated group, built on the supplied filings and releases and the earlier modules' findings, with its strongest support, weakest dimension and primary downside path.
## Sources

| EX-99.1_2026-11-02_a09302026ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl | Press release (Exhibit 99.1) reporting third quarter 2026 results | 2026-11-02 | 649e9df09c58fc28e42170873dd9e204e4698e7b6a16ba8868ab909251dcc271 | Backlog, utilisation, revenue efficiency, outlook commentary, statement on guidance |

| Financial foundation | CP-1 | d029ac09759d646fecd8de3f2f3945417ea55b80d12f77a517e30cc08d652d8b | Statements, leverage, cover, liquidity, net debt with pro forma, free cash flow and the debt schedule |

| Business & governance | CP-1A | b83a8d40bdeac3b2fb4539f19af1d08a3f17eded8eb49b5901b6ca0fd560e361 | Business, customers, backlog, ownership, combination terms, ARO exposure, governance behaviour and risk level |
No external sources were used.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Valaris presents an adequate fundamental credit profile: a contracted drillship recovery and USD 900.1 million of liquidity outweigh rising trailing leverage, but negative free cash flow and a pending change of control mean creditors should expect liquidity to erode before earnings fully recover.
Basis: calculation F8; calculation F6; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Last-twelve-month reported leverage was 2.97x and net debt was USD 563.4 million, or USD 555.9 million pro forma for the October 2026 rig sale; net leverage was 1.54x, or 1.51x pro forma. Operating cash flow less capital additions was negative USD 172.7 million in the first nine months of 2026, which is why a quarter of Adjusted EBITDA of USD 150.6 million, more than twice the first quarter's USD 66.7 million, matters more than the trailing ratio.
Basis: calculation F1; calculation F2; calculation F4; calculation F5; calculation F9; calculation F7; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Key findings

- Revenue visibility is good but concentrated. Contract backlog of USD 4,750.1 million is 2.39x last-twelve-month revenues, yet floaters hold 61.1% of it and four customers supplied 49% of Q3 revenue, so a few customers' programmes decide whether the recovery holds.
Basis: calculation K1; calculation F15; calculation F16; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Margins are recovering through operating leverage, and day rates are rising where the fleet is working. Contract drilling expenses fell from 79.1% of revenues in Q1 to 68.4% in Q3 while average daily revenue for floaters rose 19.4% in nine months, so each restarted drillship adds earnings faster than cost; the risk is that jackup day rates fell 2.2% and war-risk insurance cost USD 23.0 million more over nine months, although it eased in the third quarter.

Basis: calculation F17; calculation K2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Cash conversion is the weak point. Operating cash flow less capital additions was negative USD 172.7 million in nine months against positive USD 236.8 million a year earlier, and the 2026 capital additions range of USD 445.0 million to USD 470.0 million implies USD 117.0 million to USD 142.0 million more in the fourth quarter, so no debt has been repaid and cash has fallen by USD 74.3 million since year-end to fund maintenance, upgrade and contract-specific spending.
Basis: calculation F9; calculation F11; calculation K12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Liquidity is adequate and refinancing is a 2030 question. Liquidity of USD 900.1 million (cash of USD 525.1 million at 2026-09-30, for which a pro forma figure after the October 2026 rig sale is not established, plus the undrawn USD 375.0 million revolver) sits against no principal maturity before 2030, one secured bond of USD 1,100.0 million and a revolver due in 2028 that is undrawn; the revolver becomes a current obligation from April 2027. Its three financial covenants (equity to total assets, interest cover and minimum liquidity) have no levels printed, and the issuer reports compliance in all material respects at 2026-09-30.
Basis: calculation F8; calculation F13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-12-31_val-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 129; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Leverage is moderate and the trajectory is the risk. Reported leverage rose from 1.74x at the end of FY2025 to 2.97x as strong 2025 quarters rolled out of the twelve months, and cover on net interest expense is 3.74x, against cash interest cover of 6.89x in FY2025; trailing leverage falls at the next quarter end if fourth-quarter 2026 reported EBITDA exceeds the USD 80.0 million of the quarter it replaces, and the third quarter was USD 48.6 million above that.
Basis: calculation F1; calculation F3; calculation F12; calculation F20; calculation K10; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Governance risk is event-driven rather than extractive. There is no sponsor, no dividend and no repurchase in 2026, but a change of control is scheduled for closing on or about 2026-12-01 and ARO may call up to USD 1,100.0 million of newbuild funding; the notes' fair value of 102.3% of principal sits above the 101.0% repurchase price, so that protection would matter only if the price fell.
Basis: calculation F18; calculation F19; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- A one-year return to the first-quarter earnings level would raise net leverage to 3.08x on Adjusted EBITDA, or 3.28x on reported EBITDA, but would not exhaust liquidity. Adjusted EBITDA of USD 266.8 million, the coupon and last-twelve-month capital additions give a cash outflow of USD 259.6 million, leaving liquidity of USD 640.5 million; the scenario is illustrative and ignores cash taxes, working capital, disposals, interest income and any ARO call.
Basis: calculation K3; calculation K4; calculation K6; calculation K7; calculation K8; calculation K11
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against an adequate profile is cash conversion: free cash flow has been negative for the last twelve months while capital additions run well above operating cash flow, trailing leverage has climbed to 2.97x, and the Middle East conflicts, shipyard delays and war-risk insurance still cut operating income by about USD 24.0 million in the third quarter. The view would weaken if fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA fell back toward the first-quarter level of USD 66.7 million, if capital additions came in above USD 142.0 million for the quarter, if ARO called capital, or if the change of control left the notes in a weaker position. It would strengthen if earnings held near the third-quarter level and the combined company kept the 2026 pause on repurchases.
Basis: calculation F9; calculation F11; calculation F7; calculation F1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Limitations

- The levels of the revolver's three financial covenants (equity to total assets, interest cover and minimum liquidity) are not printed, so the finding that liquidity is adequate assumes the full facility can be drawn; if the covenants bind in a downturn, usable liquidity would be lower than stated, although the issuer reports compliance at 2026-09-30.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1)

- The downside scenario holds one quarter's earnings level for a year and ignores cash taxes, working capital, disposals, interest income and ARO calls, so its cash and leverage results indicate direction and size rather than a forecast; its leverage is shown on Adjusted and on reported EBITDA, while the headline ratios use reported EBITDA.
Basis: calculation K3
- Cash interest paid is stated only for fiscal years, so interest cover for the latest period rests on net interest expense, which can differ from cash paid, so the cover finding is approximate.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Ratings, peer data and market prices other than the quarter-end fair value of the notes were not supplied, so the finding that the profile is adequate is judged against the issuer's own history and sector description, not against peers.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)

- The shareholder meetings scheduled for 2026-11-24 and the court hearing scheduled for 2026-11-26 fall after the as-of date, so the view describes the pre-closing structure and would need to be redone on the combined group if the transaction closes.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); {src(Q3, 12)}
### Strengths and weaknesses
Strengths, ranked by weight in the credit view:

- Contracted earnings base. Backlog of USD 4,750.1 million, all ten active drillships on contract and revenue efficiency of 97% in Q3 mean the recovery rests on signed contracts, which supports debt service over several years; floaters and a handful of customers carry most of it.
Basis: calculation K1; calculation F15; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_a09302026ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_a09302026ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 11
- Liquidity and maturity profile. Liquidity of USD 900.1 million and no principal due before the 2030 notes leave time to complete the recovery without refinancing pressure.
Basis: calculation F8; calculation F13; Financial foundation (CP-1)
- Operating leverage on restarted rigs. The cost ratio fell from 79.1% to 68.4% in two quarters and floater day rates rose 19.4%, so each further restart adds earnings faster than cost.
Basis: calculation F17; calculation K2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42

- No sponsor extraction. No controlling shareholder is disclosed, no dividends have been paid and repurchases are paused until closing, which removes the usual leakage route, though it also removes any equity backstop.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_val-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 70
Weaknesses, ranked by weight in the credit view:
- Negative free cash flow. Capital additions exceed operating cash flow, so cash falls and leverage depends on earnings alone to improve.
Basis: calculation F9; calculation F11; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Customer, segment and country concentration. Four customers supplied about 49% of Q3 revenue, floaters hold 61.1% of backlog and Brazil supplied 23.1% of revenue, so one programme or tax event moves results.
Basis: calculation F15; calculation F16; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Contingent affiliate funding. Valaris may be asked for up to USD 1,100.0 million of newbuild funding if ARO cannot raise third-party finance; ARO held USD 32.1 million of cash at 2026-09-30, has paid no cash to its partners since formation and owes Valaris USD 400.7 million of notes due in October 2027 and October 2028, so cash may flow out before any flows in.
Basis: calculation F19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54

- Event and information risk. The combined company's treatment of the notes is not established, and the issuer will not hold earnings calls or update guidance before closing, so monitoring relies on filings.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-11-02_a09302026ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 5
### Business and ownership in credit terms

Valaris contracts ultra-deepwater drillships and premium jackups on day rate contracts, so earnings follow rig utilisation and day rates, and a stacked or idle rig earns nothing while its holding costs continue. The group is widely held with no sponsor, which means no committed equity support and no sponsor-driven leakage; the creditors' main exposure is the pending sale to Transocean and the 50% ARO joint venture, which Valaris does not consolidate, so ARO's own debt is outside group net debt and its earnings reach Valaris only as an equity share that Adjusted EBITDA excludes.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Revenue durability

Revenue is contracted for periods of about 1 month to 4 years, which gives visibility, but some contracts allow termination for the customer's convenience or if a final investment decision is not taken, so backlog is not guaranteed cash. Pricing is improving for floaters (average daily revenue up 19.4% over nine months) and softer for jackups (down 2.2%). For creditors, the recovery in revenue is a contracted-restart story whose realisation depends on customers' programmes.
Basis: calculation K2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2025-12-31_val-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10
### Margin resilience

Costs look largely fixed once a rig is working, so margins widen as utilisation rises and would narrow just as fast if it fell; contract drilling expenses were USD 379.9 million in Q3 against USD 380.4 million in Q2 while revenues rose from USD 502.3 million to USD 555.6 million. Over nine months expense was flat because USD 67.3 million of higher repair and maintenance cost and USD 23.0 million of higher insurance, mainly war-risk cover, were offset by USD 103.8 million of lower costs for rigs sold. Margins can be defended on volume only while utilisation stays high, and the creditor consequence is higher earnings sensitivity in both directions.
Basis: calculation F17; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_a09302026ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40
### Cash conversion and capital intensity

Capital intensity is high while idle drillships are returned to work and upgraded: nine-month capital additions of USD 328.0 million were more than twice operating cash flow of USD 155.3 million, and part of that spending is contract-specific and recoverable from customers. Operating cash flow also included about USD 43.0 million of U.S. tax refunds and asset sales brought in USD 102.6 million, while the interest on the notes is fixed. EBITDA is therefore not converting to free cash flow now, and spending is met from cash and asset sales rather than from retained earnings.
Basis: calculation F10; calculation F9; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52
### Market forces and external factors

Rivalry is strong because contracts are awarded by competitive bid and price is often the deciding factor, and ten drillships across the industry were idle at the end of the third quarter with nine due back to work by early 2027, which could cap day rates; the supply of benign environment floaters has fallen by more than 45% since 2014, which supports them. New entry is limited by high newbuild cost and shipyard capacity, substitutes are other oil supply such as onshore shale and, over time, the energy transition, buyers are a few large oil companies with termination rights, and suppliers (shipyards, insurers, crews) have pushed costs up. Politically, the Middle East conflicts cost about USD 24.0 million of operating income in Q3, and tax disputes and the 15% Bermuda tax add earnings uncertainty.
### Financial profile

On the method's nine dimensions the assessment is: scale and market position average, with a fleet the issuer describes as among the largest in the world (13 drillships and 28 jackups owned at 2026-11-03) but a concentrated customer base; competitive advantage average, resting on modern seventh-generation drillships (12 of 13) rather than on contract terms; business diversification weak to average, with floaters 61.1% of backlog; cost and capex flexibility average, because contract-specific capital spending is recoverable but a fixed cost base is not; margin stability average, improving; free cash flow stability weak; ability to refinance average, with one bond due in 2030 and market quotations not supplied beyond the quarter-end fair value; liquidity position strong relative to maturities; and financial policy and governance average, with no sponsor but event risk from the combination. Supports are the contracted base and liquidity; the main constraint is free cash flow.
Basis: calculation F15; calculation F8; calculation F9; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36
### Outlook

Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the debt-service case depends on drillship restarts continuing: management says day rates are moving higher and deepwater opportunities are converting to contracts. Reinvestment stays high, with USD 117.0 million to USD 142.0 million of capital additions still implied for the fourth quarter, and ARO has ordered four newbuild jackups that Valaris may be asked to help fund. Sector tailwinds are customer emphasis on energy security and deepwater sanctioning (about 65% of expected deepwater activity has breakeven prices below USD 50 a barrel), and headwinds are the Middle East conflicts, cost inflation and war-risk insurance. Over three to five years the 2028 revolver and the 2030 notes fall due, so the outlook for earnings through 2027 decides refinancing terms.

Basis: calculation F11; calculation F19; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_a09302026ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Downside scenario

An issuer-specific downside starts with a customer programme delay or a Middle East shipyard stoppage that returns Adjusted EBITDA to the first-quarter level of USD 66.7 million a quarter; at that level revenue and utilisation fall first, the largely fixed cost base turns the margin gain back, and free cash flow turns more negative because capital additions are committed. Holding that level for four quarters gives Adjusted EBITDA of USD 266.8 million, a coupon cover of 2.90x and a cash outflow of USD 259.6 million after the coupon and capital additions, so cash falls from USD 525.1 million at 2026-09-30 to USD 265.5 million, liquidity to USD 640.5 million and net leverage rises to 3.08x. Management can slow discretionary capital additions and sell stacked rigs, as it did in 2026, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress within twelve months, but the margin for the 2028 revolver renewal narrows and the revolver's covenants, whose levels are not printed, could become the binding constraint.
Basis: calculation K3; calculation K4; calculation K5; calculation K6; calculation K7; calculation K8; calculation K9; calculation F7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22
### Overall credit view

Overall, Valaris presents an adequate business profile supported by contracted drillship backlog, modern assets and liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by negative free cash flow, trailing leverage that has risen and concentration in customers and floaters. Cash-flow durability appears adequate only if the third-quarter earnings level holds. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on earnings through 2027 and on how the change of control treats the notes. The primary downside path is a fall back to first-quarter earnings while capital spending stays committed. Further analysis would require the indenture, the credit agreement, the acquirer's disclosure and ARO's accounts. Fundamental credit review completed with limitations. Top risk: negative free cash flow combined with event risk from the change of control.
Basis: calculation F1; calculation F9; calculation F8; calculation F7; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

## Gaps

- The levels of the revolver's three financial covenants (equity to total assets, interest cover and minimum liquidity) are not printed in the annual report or the quarterly report, which say only that the issuer complied in all material respects, so headroom is not calculated and liquidity is stated before any covenant restriction (High for the liquidity finding).
- Cash interest paid is stated only in the annual report (USD 90.5 million for FY2025), not for quarters, so latest-period cover uses net interest expense as a proxy (Medium).

- The scenario inputs are an analyst choice: the first-quarter Adjusted EBITDA level held for four quarters, the coupon and last-twelve-month capital additions; it excludes cash taxes, working capital, disposals, interest income and any ARO call (Medium).
- Ratings, peer data and market prices other than the quarter-end fair value of the notes were not supplied, so the profile is not compared with peers (Medium).
- The proxy statement, the indenture and the credit agreement were not supplied, so governance and capacity conclusions rest on observed behaviour (Medium).
- Pro forma cash for the October 2026 rig sale is not established, so cash and liquidity are stated as at 2026-09-30 (Low).
- Page numbers cited in this analysis are chunk numbers of the supplied text files, not printed page numbers (Low).
